subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A reaction reaches equilibrium only in a:
questions.explain: Equilibrium can only be reached in a closed system where nothing can enter or escape.

questions.q: If the forward reaction of a reversible reaction is endothermic, what is the reverse reaction?
questions.explain: If the forward direction is endothermic, the reverse direction releases the same energy, so it is exothermic.

questions.q: How many moles are in 36 g of water, H2O? (Mr = 18)
questions.explain: moles = mass/Mr = 36/18 = 2 mol.

questions.q: What is the concentration in mol/dm³ of a solution with 0.5 mol of solute in 2 dm³?
questions.explain: concentration = moles/volume = 0.5/2 = 0.25 mol/dm³.

questions.q: Which process is endothermic and is used in instant cold packs?
options: Dissolving certain salts such as ammonium nitrate
questions.explain: Dissolving ammonium nitrate takes in energy from the surroundings, cooling the pack.

questions.q: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 50 g but only 40 g is obtained. What is the percentage yield?
questions.explain: percentage yield = (40/50)×100 = 80%.

questions.q: Which subatomic particle is found outside the nucleus?
questions.explain: Electrons occupy shells (energy levels) outside the nucleus.

questions.q: Why is diamond unable to conduct electricity?
options: Its layers slide over each other
It has no charged particles free to move
questions.explain: In diamond every electron is held in a covalent bond, so none are free to carry charge.

questions.q: Chlorine has two isotopes: 75% chlorine-35 and 25% chlorine-37. What is its relative atomic mass?
Why does a reaction generally slow down over time even without changing conditions?
options: The reactant concentration decreases as it is used up
questions.explain: As reactants are consumed, their concentration falls, so collisions are less frequent and the rate decreases.

questions.q: For an ionic compound to act as an electrolyte it must be:
questions.explain: Ions must be free to move, which only happens when the ionic compound is molten or in solution.

questions.q: Why do simple molecular substances have low melting and boiling points?
questions.explain: Only weak intermolecular forces need to be overcome, not the strong covalent bonds.

questions.q: At the anode during electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride, the product is:
questions.explain: When a halide ion is present, the halogen (chlorine) is produced at the anode rather than oxygen.

questions.q: A rechargeable cell differs from a non-rechargeable cell because:
options: Its reactions can be reversed by an external current
questions.explain: Recharging reverses the cell reactions by applying an external current, restoring the reactants.

questions.q: Why is the relative mass of an electron taken as very small?
options: An electron's mass is negligible compared with a proton or neutron
questions.explain: An electron's mass is about 1/1836 of a proton's, so it is treated as negligible.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an exothermic process?
options: Neutralisation of an acid and alkali
questions.explain: Neutralisation releases energy, so the temperature of the mixture rises — it is exothermic.

questions.q: In the electrolysis of aqueous sodium sulfate, what forms at the cathode?
questions.explain: Sodium is more reactive than hydrogen, so hydrogen is discharged at the cathode.

questions.q: Is bond breaking endothermic or exothermic?
questions.explain: Breaking bonds requires energy to be supplied, so it is endothermic.

questions.q: How does increasing temperature increase the rate of reaction?
options: Particles move faster and collide more often with more energy
questions.explain: Higher temperature gives particles more energy, so they collide more frequently and more energetically.

questions.q: When magnesium burns, the mass appears to increase. Why?
options: The magnesium gives off a gas
Oxygen from the air combines with the magnesium
questions.explain: Oxygen from the air joins the magnesium to form magnesium oxide, so the solid mass increases.

questions.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom concentrated?
options: In the empty space around the nucleus
questions.explain: Protons and neutrons in the nucleus contain nearly all the atom's mass.

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a proton?
questions.explain: Protons carry a relative charge of +1.
